result.topic_en: Brief notes on the integral of dz/z in polar form (log r + phi i) and on splitting a definite integral of dz/z from 1 into two pieces, with a small sketch of axes.
result.transcription:
$\int \frac{\partial z}{z} = \int\left(\frac{\partial r}{r} + \partial\varphi\, i\right) = \log r[?] + \varphi i$

[sketch: vertical and horizontal axes with a short slanted line rising from the horizontal axis]

$\int_1^{s} \frac{\partial z}{z} = \psi(s)$
$\int_1^{ss'} \frac{\partial z}{\partial z}[?] = \int_1^{s} \frac{\partial z}{z} + \int_{s}^{ss'} \frac{\partial z}{z}$

methods.what: Integral of dz/z in polar coordinates z = r e^{i phi}, giving the complex logarithm log r + i phi
Defining a function as the integral of dz/z from 1 to s
Additivity of the integral of dz/z over [1, ss'], split at s (toward the functional equation of the logarithm)
